original_question: For semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, does the violation of locality occur for generic potentials V, or only for specially chosen potentials?
target_in_paper: §2.1, unnumbered follow-up immediately after Question 2: after posing the higher-dimensional existence problem for sums of the form Σ_j |E_j|^{-σ}δ(E_j)^{γ+σ} ≫ ħ^{-d} as ħ→0, the authors ask whether the resulting violation of locality is generic in V or only occurs for specially chosen potentials. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right operator class (semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials) and the right qualitative issue (whether locality-violating behavior is generic or exceptional). It is aimed at the correct place in the paper: the unnumbered open-ended question in §2.1 that follows Question 2. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
missing_details: The operator should be specified as H_{ħ,V} = -ħ²Δ + V on L²(ℝ^d), with ħ∈(0,1], under the paper’s standing assumptions that V is locally sufficiently regular and decays at infinity so that the spectrum outside [0,∞) consists of isolated eigenvalues E_j of finite algebraic multiplicity. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The relevant quantity is not an unspecified spectral statistic: in §1.2 and §2.1 the paper studies sums Σ_j |E_j|^{-σ}δ(E_j)^{γ+σ}, where δ(E)=dist(E,[0,∞)). ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

Here violation of locality is tied to failure of the semiclassical/locality scale ħ^{-d}; more concretely, the issue is whether the above sum can be much larger than ħ^{-d} as ħ→0. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the nearby official parameter regime is the one in Question 2: d≥2, γ>0, 0≤σ≤d/2, and V∈L^{γ+d/2}(ℝ^d). ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The draft does not mention that known concrete examples at this stage of the paper are only in dimension d=1; higher-dimensional analogues are exactly what Question 2 asks for. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The paper leaves generic intentionally informal here; it does not specify Baire-genericity, prevalence, or a probabilistic notion, so a refined question should not invent one. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The same sentence also asks how the power of ħ in the growth depends on the choice of V; omitting that loses part of the authors’ stated intent. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

This is not a numbered conjecture or theorem in the paper but an unnumbered follow-up comment after Question 2, so the rewritten version should preserve that narrow scope rather than broadening it into a general classification problem. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
refined_question: For the semiclassical Schrödinger operator H_{ħ,V}=-ħ²Δ+V on L²(ℝ^d), with complex-valued V satisfying the paper’s standing assumptions so that the discrete spectrum outside [0,∞) consists of eigenvalues E_j counted with algebraic multiplicity, and with δ(E)=dist(E,[0,∞)), in the regime relevant to Question 2—namely d≥2, γ>0, 0≤σ≤d/2, and V∈L^{γ+d/2}(ℝ^d)—is the locality-violating behavior Σ_j |E_j|^{-σ}δ(E_j)^{γ+σ} ≫ ħ^{-d} as ħ→0 a generic phenomenon in V, or does it occur only for specially constructed potentials; and to what extent does the resulting power of ħ depend on the choice of V? ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
justification: The draft is not best matched to Question 1 or Question 3. It matches the unnumbered sentence in §2.1 on page 3 that comes immediately after Question 2. The paper first defines locality through bounds at the semiclassical scale ħ^{-d} and the additivity of disjoint pieces of the potential, then reviews one-dimensional examples where sums of the form Σ_j |E_j|^{-σ}δ(E_j)^β exceed that scale, next asks in Question 2 whether analogous higher-dimensional examples exist, and then explicitly asks whether such violation is generic in V or only happens for specially chosen potentials, together with how the ħ-growth depends on V. The refined question therefore keeps the exact eigenvalue functional, the semiclassical scale, and the Question 2 parameter window, rather than broadening the issue to an unspecified notion of nonlocality. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

citations.label: Background; definition of H_{ħ,V}, standing assumptions, and discrete eigenvalues E_j
Meaning of locality via additive contribution of disjoint pieces of V and the semiclassical scale ħ^{-d}
Unnumbered follow-up after Question 2 on whether locality violation is generic in V or only for specially chosen potentials
Explanation that loss of locality means bounds become non-additive and involve a power of ħ larger than the semiclassical one
